plan.estimand: Minimum development sample size for survival prediction model meeting Riley criteria: precision for outcome-risk predictions via apparent versus adjusted R-squared shrinkage.
plan.hypothesis: Fitted model performance will retain 90% of apparent discrimination after external validation; shrinkage applied to calibration curve and probability predictions.
assumptions: Survival data follow Cox proportional hazards model with constant hazard over prediction horizon (2 years).
Adjusted Cox-Snell R² = 0.051 (validation-adjusted, representing model discrimination after accounting for optimism).
Event rate is constant 0.065 per person-year over the cohort follow-up and prediction horizon.
Mean follow-up 2.07 years applies uniformly to estimate person-years at risk.
Shrinkage factor 0.90 applied to calibration intercept and slope; predicted probabilities adjusted by shrinkage to reduce overfitting.
Precision criterion (max R² difference 0.05 on Nagelkerke scale) reflects acceptable loss from apparent to adjusted discrimination.
Outcome-risk margin of error 0.05 (absolute) targets ±5% interval width for predicted survival probabilities at 2-year horizon.
pmsampsize 1.1.3 default method: Riley (2020) for survival models, implemented via exponential distribution approximation or empirical calibration.
No missing data, uniform censoring mechanism, no competing risks.
Prediction model will be developed and internally validated on same sample (internal validation only; external validation is future stage).
missing_information: Confirmation: Does 'default package criteria' refer to pmsampsize::pmsampsize with event_rate as per-person-year rate and default method='riley' for survival? (Yes assumed.)
Confirmation: Does 'maximum absolute apparent-versus-adjusted R-squared difference 0.05 (Nagelkerke scale)' refer to the 'criteria' parameter in pmsampsize? (Yes assumed.)

Clarification: For verification of outcome-risk margin of error at returned sample size—do you want binomial-normal 95% CI width for probability predictions at 2-year horizon, or do you want the specific calibration-slope scenario margin for the shrunk model?
clarification_questions: Outcome-risk margin of error verification at returned N: Do you want this computed as half-width of a 95% CI for predicted risk at 2 years, assuming binomial variation? (e.g., SE = sqrt(p(1-p)/N) type formula, which depends on expected risk distribution.)
Shrinkage application: Does the 0.90 shrinkage factor apply to calibration (intercept + slope) or only to slope, per Riley method?
scientific_notes: Riley et al. (2020, Stat Methods Med Res) recommend for survival: minimum events = k(p+1)/R² where k ≈ 20 for CI-based optimism correction with shrinkage factor λ.
Nagelkerke R² for survival uses D-statistic scaled to [0,1]; Harrell's C-index and calibration-in-the-large are complementary precision metrics.
Margin of error for outcome risk 0.05 in survival context typically implies 95% CI half-width ≤ 0.05, which constrains both sample size and event count.
pmsampsize may return either total sample size or event count; verification will specify both and confirm which is binding constraint.
Shrinkage λ = 0.90 is modest; full shrinkage λ = 1.0 implies no penalty. Higher shrinkage (e.g., 0.70) is more conservative.
